findings.title: Plugin request logs lose traceID
findings.body: "Plugin Request Completed" used to include traceID from tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false), so every valid trace (sampled or not) was on the log line. That field was removed and is not added by ContextualLoggerMiddleware, which only sets endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, and uname. The new call is logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...) and Info does not take a context.Context, so the infra logger cannot recover the span at log time. Plugin request logs can no longer be correlated with traces, including unsampled ones that metrics exemplars (requireSampled=true) never recorded.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext discards recorded logs
findings.body: LoggerMiddleware now emits the completion line via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...). TestLogger.FromContext ignores the receiver and returns NewTestLogger(), a different object whose InfoLogs/WarnLogs/ErrorLogs are not the instance tests hold. Calls, message, and key/value pairs are silently dropped, so assertions on the injected test logger see zero logs even when a request was logged. The fake also ignores ctx, so it cannot observe the contextual attributes this change depends on.

findings.title: No test locks the moved contextual log fields
findings.body: Contextual attributes were moved out of the metrics middleware into instrumentContext, and completion logs now depend on a separate middleware having called log.WithContextualAttributes before LoggerMiddleware.FromContext. Nothing in this change asserts that QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, and CollectMetrics attach endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, and uname, or that "Plugin Request Completed" still emits them (and traceID). The renamed metrics test only checks Prometheus counters. A middleware reorder, a FromContext miss, or a dropped field would ship unnoticed.
